title: Semi-Markovian switching in a fluctuating harmonic trap: An age-structured formulation
abstract: We study a Brownian particle in a harmonic trap whose stiffness switches between two values with arbitrary waiting-time statistics, generating semi-Markovian dynamics. To treat the resulting temporal memory, we formulate the problem in an enlarged age-structured state space, restoring Markovianity and yielding a local Fokker--Planck description. Within this framework, we derive exact steady-state integral equations for the spatial and birth distributions and obtain exact expressions for stationary moments, injected power, and potential energy. In the second part of the paper, we analyze the stochastic-resetting limit, corresponding to a particle alternately released and trapped. By representing the stationary spatial distribution as a superposition of Gaussian states with fluctuating variance, the problem can be reformulated as a switching process in variance space. This yields exact integral equations for the variance distributions and leads to a simplified description amenable to direct analytical treatment.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theoretical framework using age-structured methods to model Brownian particles undergoing switching between harmonic traps with arbitrary memory effects. It derives exact integral equations for steady states and demonstrates that while equilibrium energy remains fixed, non-Markovian switching protocols significantly alter the injected power and spatial fluctuations. This work is valuable for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in systems with complex temporal correlations.
main_problem: Developing a general theoretical framework for analyzing semi-Markovian switching dynamics in fluctuating potentials with arbitrary waiting-time distributions.
main_result: The study derives exact integral equations and shows that while average potential energy remains at equilibrium values, injected power and spatial fluctuations are highly sensitive to the temporal memory encoded in the switching statistics.
method: The core methodology involves formulating the problem in an enlarged age-structured state space to restore Markovianity for non-exponential waiting times, followed by analyzing reduced dynamics in both position and variance spaces.
model_or_system: A Brownian particle confined by a harmonic trap whose stiffness fluctuates between two values ($K_1$ and $K_2$), leading to semi-Markovian switching dynamics. The analysis covers regimes from memoryless Markovian processes to complex stochastic-resetting limits.

important_parameters: Mean residence times ($	au_i$), stiffness values ($K_1, K_2$), and memory parameters encoded in the waiting-time distributions.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes finite mean residence times for the switching process; energy observables are governed by a generalized virial relation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $\pi(s)$ (variance distribution) comparisons for exponential, deterministic, and algebraic waiting-time protocols, and show spatial distributions $n_i(x)$ confirming asymptotic predictions for algebraic tails.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the age-structured Fokker-Planck description to handle memory. It then analyzes steady-state observables (moments, fluxes) in this extended space. Finally, it tackles specific limits, notably the variance-space formulation for stochastic resetting and analyzing moment equations.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools (age-structuring, variance dynamics) to analyze non-equilibrium transport phenomena driven by complex temporal correlations, which is highly relevant for understanding energy dissipation in open quantum systems or active matter.
